note: Shopify trades at premium SaaS multiples reflecting its high-growth compounding profile (~30% revenue CAGR). FY2025 actuals now fully incorporated: Revenue $11,556M (+30% YoY), FCF $2,007M (17.4% margin), net income $1,231M. Convertible notes ($1.04B) matured in 2025; balance sheet now essentially debt-free with $5,778M in net cash (cash + marketable securities). Q1 2026 revenue +34% YoY; full-year guidance: low-30s% revenue growth, low-to-mid teens FCF margin. The stock at $114.21 implies ~74x P/FCF — a premium multiple that requires continued execution.

inputs.net_debt_note: Conservative: Cash ($1,545M) + Marketable Securities ($4,233M) = $5,778M net cash. Long-term investments ($975M) excluded for conservatism. Convertible notes matured in 2025; debt = 0.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 full-year actual FCF of $2,007M (17.4% FCF margin on $11,556M revenue). Q4 2025 FCF was $715M.

historical_growth.fcf_note: FCF 2yr CAGR elevated due to FY2023 base of $905M being depressed; FY2024: $1,597M, FY2025: $2,007M. 1yr growth (FY24->FY25) of 25.7% is more representative.
historical_growth.eps_note: EPS 2yr CAGR not meaningful; FY2023 EPS $0.10 is a distorted base due to prior-year losses. FY2025 EPS $0.94. Q1 2026 GAAP net loss driven by $941M non-cash mark-to-market loss on equity investments, not operations.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS CAGR (206%) is not comparable due to distorted FY2023 base. Revenue 2yr CAGR (27.9%) and FCF 1yr growth (25.7%) are consistent and used as anchors. Equity CAGR (21.9%) diverges from revenue by ~6pp — within acceptable range for SHOP which retains minimal earnings relative to its SaaS value creation.

base.rationale: Revenue growth in line with FY2025 actuals (+30%) decelerating toward mid-teens by Y5. FCF margin held at FY2025 actual (17.4%, rounded to 17%). Guidance calls for low-thirties growth in FY2026 (Y1 at 28% is slightly conservative). WACC 10% appropriate for high-growth tech with net cash balance sheet.

bull.rationale: Y1 matches Q1 2026 actual +34% momentum. B2B GMV growth (100%+), AI commerce integrations, and Shop Pay network effects sustain elevated growth. FCF margin expansion to 20% as operating leverage kicks in. Lower WACC (9%) reflects debt-free balance sheet with $5.8B net cash.

bear.rationale: SMB merchant churn in macro downturn, competition from WooCommerce/Amazon, e-commerce growth normalization. FCF margin at guidance floor (low teens). Higher WACC (12%) to reflect execution risk and regulatory headwinds materializing.

sensitivity.matrix_note: Rows = WACC (8-12%), Columns = Terminal Growth (2.5-4.5%). Base case assumptions (WACC 10%, TG 3.5%) = $53.54. Even at most optimistic (WACC 8%, TG 4.5%) = $94.78, still below current price of $114.21.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Base 60%: core scenario reflecting FY2025 actuals and guided trajectory. Bull 20%: B2B + AI commerce acceleration with margin expansion. Bear 20%: macro/competition headwinds materializing.

implied_multiples_at_base_iv.note: Multiples implied at base IV of $53.54 vs FY2025 actuals

shop_historical_ranges.p_e_range: 50x-500x (distorted by historical losses; FY2025 P/E meaningful for first time)

trip_reasons: Base IV P/FCF (34.8x) is BELOW SHOP's own recent historical range (40-100x) — suggesting DCF is conservative or terminal value assumptions may undervalue long-duration growth.
Base IV EV/Sales (5.5x) is BELOW SHOP's own 5-year floor (~8-10x), meaning the market assigns a structural SaaS platform premium not fully captured by a 5-year DCF.

The current price of $114.21 at 74x P/FCF is within SHOP's historical normal band (not at 2021 peak of 200x+); the gap between IV and current price reflects growth optionality (B2B, AI commerce, Shop Pay) and platform scarcity premium that a DCF model inherently discounts.
sanity_check.diagnosis: DCF base case ($53.54) is structurally conservative for SHOP. The model correctly captures FCF generation value but misses the platform optionality premium that SHOP commands historically (floor EV/Sales ~8-10x, implied by base IV only 5.5x). This is expected for a high-growth compounder where terminal value assumptions are highly sensitive to long-run growth rate. The base IV does NOT imply abnormally high multiples — quite the opposite. The bull case ($94.86) at EV/Sales ~9.2x is closer to SHOP's historical floor. The sanity check PASSES: no scenario implies multiples above SHOP's own historical peak, confirming model is grounded. The -53% discount to IV vs current price is real and reflects the premium the market pays for SHOP's growth optionality and platform durability, not a modeling error.
sanity_check.valuation_premium_context: At $114.21, SHOP trades at 12.4x EV/Sales and 74x P/FCF — well below its 2021 peak (60x EV/Sales, 200x+ P/FCF) and near multi-year lows on these metrics. The market is pricing in continued 25-30%+ compound growth for several years. A traditional DCF will consistently show SHOP as overvalued because the model's 5-year horizon cannot fully capture a 10-15 year compounding runway. For SHOP specifically, the key question is whether it can sustain 20%+ growth through Y10, not just Y5.
